verification.detail: The targeted retention regressions completed successfully on the base commit.
The targeted retention regressions completed on the PR head and reproduced the bounded-memory violation.

findings.claim: Moving retention trimming before batch processing preserves the 10,000-entry bounded-memory behavior.
findings.affected_behavior: Batch ingestion can retain more than 10,000 logs after add_logs returns.

evidence.detail: Temporary batch-retention regressions failed on PR head and passed on main.
evidence.head: FAIL

evidence.detail: The PR trims using only pre-batch length and then inserts the full batch without another capacity check.

findings.expected: Retained logs remain at or below 10,000 after batch ingestion.
findings.observed: A 9,999-entry state plus two entries retains 10,001; a single 15,000-entry batch retains 15,000.
reproduction: Create AppState::new(None), add 9,999 entries, then add two entries and assert logs.len() <= 10_000.
Create AppState::new(None), add one 15,000-entry batch and assert logs.len() <= 10_000.
Run the same temporary tests on PR head and main.
attempted_disproof: Searched add_logs/add_log callers for a batch-size constraint; none exists.
Searched for a post-batch retention guard; none exists.
Ran identical tests on main; both passed there.
Tested filtered indexes and tail state at the trim boundary; that separate hypothesis did not reproduce.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Real-world frequency and memory impact depend on batch size; the retention violation is reproduced.
